headline: Bitcoin breaks below $57,000 for the first time in two years as Fear & Greed hits extreme fear.
summary: Bitcoin breached a critical multi-year support level on Friday, touching below $57,000 intraday before recovering to $60,283 at the snapshot — its lowest territory since late 2024. The move dragged nearly every major asset lower, with Ethereum falling 3.5% and BNB dropping over 4%. The one exception was Monero, which gained 3.45% even as a $13 million hack wiped out a wrapped Monero token, suggesting traders moved into spot XMR as a privacy-coin hedge.

winners.name: Monero
winners.catalyst: Monero gained amid broad market weakness, likely driven by privacy-coin demand as Bitcoin slid below $57,000 and fear intensified. The rally is notable despite the Wagyu XMR1 wrapped Monero hack ($13M loss), suggesting spot XMR demand outweighed the wrapped-token contagion.

losers.name: MemeCore
losers.catalyst: No specific catalyst identified; the decline likely reflects amplified selling pressure on lower-liquidity assets during a broad risk-off session.

whyItMoved:
Bitcoin's intraday break below $57,000 — a level not seen since late 2024 — was the day's defining event. The move is not a single-catalyst story; several pressures converged. ETF outflows have been mounting through November, steadily draining institutional demand. Nvidia's stock fell to a 52-week low after reports of an SEC accounting probe, amplifying risk-off sentiment across both tech and crypto — the two asset classes have moved in close correlation this cycle. JPMorgan analysts added a structural note: BTC is now trading well below their estimated $86,000 miner production cost, a gap that historically signals financial stress for mining operations and raises questions about long-term hash rate stability.

Ethereum's 3.5% decline carried its own secondary concern. Treasury firm BTCS disclosed to the SEC that its $54 million ETH-collateralized position on the DeFi lending platform Aave faces liquidation risk as ETH prices fall. If that position is liquidated, it would add forced selling pressure to an already weak market — a dynamic that has amplified past downturns. The Fear & Greed Index at 12 (extreme fear) reflects how broadly this concern has spread.

The one exception was Monero, up 3.45%. A $13 million hack destroyed the XMR1 wrapped Monero token, but native XMR held up and gained — a pattern consistent with traders moving into the underlying asset when a derivative product fails.
worthKnowing: BTCS disclosed to the SEC that its $54 million ETH-collateralized Aave position faces liquidation risk, raising concerns about DeFi liquidation cascades if Ethereum continues to fall.
JPMorgan estimates Bitcoin's miner production cost at $86,000 — BTC is now trading roughly 30% below that level, intensifying pressure on mining operations.
Wagyu's XMR1 wrapped Monero token collapsed 99% after a $13 million exploit; the project's founder has promised refunds to affected holders.
Nvidia fell to a 52-week low after reports of an SEC accounting probe, contributing to risk-off pressure that spilled into crypto markets.
